html:
Under the ground in the west of Almera is the monastery of Ulyana Sad. His novices dig endless tunnels and can say only a few words a day. Angry, unhappy Nora, who everyone calls Plaxoy, gets a new partner. She barely keeps on her feet, almost does not speak, but knows much more about life upstairs than you might expect from such a girl.

The interlude is written on behalf of Nora: the reader sees the new girl only through her eyes and, like Nora herself, does not know for a long time that she is the heroine of the first novel before him. The first chapters are told in the past tense, the scenes of the meal and prayer are told in the present.

Setting

The monastery is dug in clay and consists of several “circles”. The novices live in the lower circle: there are two chapels, a refectory, a kitchen, a water tank with rain runoff, latrines, a tunnel for trolleys and several dozen cells. The vault of the chapel of the lower circle is carved from milk marble and illuminated by sixteen lamps. Older sisters live in the upper circle, where there are outlets for sunlight and rainwater in the ceiling. They serve memorial services and see parishioners. The officials of the monastery, the prioress and her assistants, go upstairs on the affairs of the monastery. The abbot owns half a dozen villages with all the income, and her power Nora compares to the power of a small lord.

Each novice is allowed five words a day. For extra words, they are punished by deprivation of lunch and light, and informers are encouraged. Eating at night and taking food out of the refectory is prohibited. Late to the pre-dinner prayer in the refectory is not allowed. Candles, oil and in general everything that can burn is valued in the caves more than silver, and for an extra candle, according to Nora, you can exchange an apple or a loaf of warm water. The cells of the partners are connected by an outlet. According to Cindy, once the novices lived in twos, but after one pair, which caught the Prioress, the cells were made single.

Prayers are addressed to the Mother Ulyana Sad, the “sister of death”. They celebrate the "cold light": wisdom, quiet joy and peace, which are contrasted with the "hot flame" of passions and the "cold darkness" of despair. The morning prayer is called “Thanks to the Sad Ulyana”. Before the meal, the Virginia Prioress, "endowed with voice", asks Foremother to send the sisters a cold light.

Plot

Novenkaya

In August 1774, Sister Jen leads to a dead end, where Nora, a newcomer, works. She arrived only on the third day, and no one except Plaxa would want to take her as a couple. Nora presents herself in three words and immediately scolds herself for profligacy, and the new girl answers with one: “Mia” and bows. The new one is exhausted: fallen cheeks, black shadows under the eyes, waxy skin. So Sister Jen gives her the shovel, and Nora tells her to wear buckets to the trolley. In an hour, Mia barely fills one bucket. Nora does not feel pity for her, only angry envy. “I am sick” everyone will regret, she will be given an extra piece, and maybe a whole candle. In the evening, Sister Jen finds work insufficient. When Nora blames her partner, the nun nods on the second shoulder blade: “Would help.” Nora and Cindy are assigned to wash dishes out of turn.

During the meal, Cindy Sudeisha, the fourth daughter of the junior judge from Clermi, demands that Nora find out from the new news from above. At the evening prayer, Mia spends a word to say "Beautiful" about the marble vault. Nora despises her for this: to talk about the beauty of the place, when the soul is full of the bliss of prayer, can only be an empty person.

The Secret of Plaxes

Nora cried in the caves for six weeks in a row, although the rest of the novices stop crying after half a month. Therefore, she is considered a fool and a “powerless sheep.” On the forty-fifth day, during the evening prayer for the "torment of unrequited feelings", Nora had a dream: to die. Since then, she has been crying less and thinking about ways. She tried to cut her hand three times with a shovel, but did not have the will. There are no knives in the refectory, and novices are not allowed in the kitchen. The pits, apart from the latrines, are not in the caves, and the cistern is only one and a half feet deep. There was a stone.

One day, Nora asks Mia with hope if she has a moron: she hopes to get infected. Mia replies, "The poison. Put it in coffee.” Nora thinks it's a lie. A cup of coffee costs two agates, more than the best wine, and no one will waste poison on a frozen girl who is destined to rot underground. When Mia faints, Nora kisses her on the lips, looks into her eyes, and breathes into her breath to make sure she catches the infection. When Mia wakes up, she says seven extra words. Nora shows five fingers and seven more, gets a piece of ham for a denunciation, and Mia is left without lunch. At night, Nora listens through the outlet as a hungry neighbor rushes around the cell, and is angry that she never cried.

Stone

Mia's getting better. She herself asks to wear buckets, quickly returns and draws a trolley with toothed "pancakes" - gears with a blade on clay. Nora decides that the fever at the new woman's mind has become confused. At the same time, Nora notices a large cobblestone in the dead end vault, barely protruding from the clay. The morning prayer for the “miraculous clarity” of the cold light finally convinces her: this is the goal and the road to it. She changes jobs with Mia and starts digging slyly. It deepens the middle of the passage, and leaves earthen protrusions on the edges on which the stone rests.

The target softens Nora. She is ready to believe that Mia foolishly ate rat poison, and, enjoying the feeling of superiority, slips her a piece of cheese at lunch. Mia explains her hunger by the fact that she did not eat for almost a month because of the poison. But soon Nora is gripped by longing: she will die, and no one will shed tears on her. The question is, “Why don’t you cry?” Mia replies, “I cry. Quiet." From that day on, Nora spends every day on the story of her beloved Jerry: strong, wore it like a fluff, called it “tiny” and “sun”, for him she ran away from home. Mia seems not to listen and asks about her: what are they building in the caves and when they take out the trolleys. Nora replies that the trolleys leave when they are full, during lunch. Later, Mia herself asks to tell about Jerry and thanks for each answer.

Night in the dark

Mia asks Sister Jen for a prayer book. An illiterate nun checks her, pointing to the words she learns herself, and Mia easily reads: “Premater”, “Death”, “Light”. The stone is ready by this time: its weight lies on two thickening walls, and two blows with a blade are enough. On that day, Mia is late for the pre-lunch prayer, and the refectory doors are locked. Nora, out of compassion, hides bread and cheese for her under the balahon. Cindy catches her, and the girls mock: “Dinner in bed for the lady!”, “Don’t forget coffee, she loves!” The food is taken away, and both partners are taken out of the candles.

In the darkness, Mia speaks through an outlet, not counting words, and herself proves the story of Nora. Jerry was a noble squire. He fell in love with another, Nora became a burden to him, tried to keep him caresses and pleas, and it was he who sent her to the caves. Nora answers only "yes", getting louder, almost breaking into a scream. Mia says, “I’m sorry. I hope you believe.”

Collapse

In the morning, Mia leaves with a bucket, and Nora stands under a stone and raises the blade. Mia returns too quickly and threatens to call her sister Jen. Nora threatens to extradite her in return: she realized that the new girl is not crazy, but is preparing an escape and therefore studies the trolleys. While Mia asks "Why?...", Nora stabs the blade in the supports. The stone moves too slowly: Mia manages to pull Nora out from under it, and both fall to the ground. Nora is furious and grabs the savior by the throat, but hears footsteps. Mia explains to the escaped sisters that there was a collapse and Nora saved her. Girls are told to clear the rubble, but lunch is not deprived.

Nora embraces indifference. Mia, encountering her in the hallway, whispers about life upstairs: there are August, apples and cherries playing weddings. She finally reveals the plan. The wagon is not unloaded by people: it turns on its own gears. If you're late for dinner, the wagons will leave, and they'll be grabbed when they're far away. To Nora's cry that she would have no other chance of dying, Mia replies that she would have a choice upstairs. Like life - will live, and not like - Mia will kill her: "I know how."

Escape

Mia brings Nora into the hall, where there are three trolleys on the rails, tells her to lie down in one of the carriages, covered with earth, and gives her a breathing tube, rolled up from sheets torn from the prayer book. Mia buries Nora with clay and promises to lie next to her. But she's caught by Virginia's Prioress. Mia explains that she is interested in the device of the trolley, and she is sent to the cell without light and without lunch. The novices pour over Nora several more buckets, and in horror from the burial alive, she realizes that she does not want to die anymore. The carriage's moving.

At sunset, Nora dumps on a huge pile of land in an old quarry. Blinded by the light, she climbs the path and cries without shame for the first time in three months. She realizes that she has deprived Mia of a chance: she will be found missing and the path will be closed. Nora rehearses five words she would say if she could: “Forgive me, fool,” “I will remember you forever,” “I believe in you all.” None of it's good. She finally finds what she needs:

“I promise I will keep your gift.”

Her car stops behind her. A good-natured moustached peasant laughs at her appearance, puts her to his side and stretches out a bundle of food.

Characters

  • Nora (Plaksa) is a low circle novice, a storyteller. Caught in the caves about three months ago: she was sent there by her lover who abandoned her. He dreams of death and eventually runs free instead of Mia.
  • Mia is a new novice. (Minerva) Her real name has never been revealed, but this is Minerva Stagforth, who survived the poisoning. (Attempt on Mira's Life) She is smart, very hungry and never smiles.
  • Sister Jen is a work overseer. Illiterate, strict, but heartwarming: at breakfast gives Mia extra edge.
  • Prioress Virginia is a "voice-endowed" sister who prays.
  • Cindy Sudeisha is a confident and beautiful novice, the fourth daughter of a junior judge from Clermie. He lives in the caves for two years, and everyone is waiting for her to become an older sister.
  • Jerry is a squire, Nora's former lover. It only appears in her memories.
  • A mustache farmer picks up Nora on the road.

Relationship with other books

In the text of the interlude, Mia is never called by her real name. However, her story about the poison in coffee and the circumstances of imprisonment directly continue the finale of Arrow, Coin, Spark. There, Gallard Almera offers Mira, who holds the conspirators under the crossbow, the cave monastery of St. Ulyana in the west of Almera: "You can't speak, but you will save your life."

In "Only One Star" the way of the monastery is already described by the eyes of Mira: in the lower circle of thirty-eight novices, five words a day, the offender loses dinner, and then the day candle. Myra spent her five words before going to bed saying, “Blessed be the Mother of Ulyana the Sad.” It also mentions the names of prayers and Abbess Delia. From the monastery, the people of Vittor Shayland, Inge Price and Sir Francis Murray (Ef) are taken away. (Inzhi Price; Eff) Rebecca Litland solved the cipher in a farewell note to a friend (see "The Soul of the West"), but her father locked her under a lock, and Ethan realized that you can take the girl from the monastery only by order of the emperor. Rumors of imprisonment reached Vittor, he solved the game Sybil Northwood, found Mira and brought to Waymar as a blackmail weapon. In Waymar, Mira recalls: “My first partner was Nora. She was dumber than a goat and cry like a baby, but I felt her almost like my own kin. Later, she mentally remembers the “bad cry of Nora”.

Significance in the Series

The interlude shows the heroine of the first novel from the outside, through the eyes of a stranger and at first a person hostile to her. The world in it is not only smart, but also generous. She spends her only chance to escape to save the girl who reported on her. Here is described in detail the life of the monasteries of Pramatery Ulyana Sad: a vow of little words, underground works, the "cold light" of the Sad Pramatery. (Foremothers) These monasteries will reappear in the next interlude, The Soul of the West, where Becca Litland, on a farewell note from a friend, guesses where she is imprisoned.

Trivia

  • Nora pretends to be a connoisseur of disease: "mor", in her opinion, is transmitted with breathing, look or words, so she kisses an insensitive Mia.
  • Mia hides her class, but utters all the behavior: bows, thanks, knows how to read and knows what a gear is. She is mocked as “the lady” and “the rich woman” without knowing that she has guessed.
  • In "Only One Star" the monastery is placed "in the west of Blackmore County", while in "Plax" and in the first novel - in the west of Almera.
